title: Query lower bound for three-bit majority
statement: Let $T$ be a decision tree on three coordinates with sign-valued inputs and outputs, and suppose it computes the majority function on three signs, with ties assigned the positive sign. There exist a coordinate $i\in\{0,1,2\}$ and a map $j:\{−1,1\}\to\{0,1,2\}$ such that $j(a)\ne i$ for each sign $a$. For every input $x\in\{−1,1\}^3$, the number of queries made by $T$ is at least $2$ if $x_i=x_{j(x_i)}$, and at least $3$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ is a decision tree on three coordinates with sign inputs and outputs
$T$ computes three-coordinate majority, with nonnegative sum mapped to positive sign
